subject: chemistry_2
question_text: Write any two ores with formulae of the following metals: a) Al b) Zn c) Fe d) Cu

verification.note: Unit 6 (Metallurgy) is sourced from the chemistry half of "FAST TRACK IPE for Sr. Students", book pp.79-82, which prints the question and a model answer. The 1+1 mark split is a CLAIM, not the board's, until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it; the question itself is sourced, not invented. Neither the two-book union check nor a board back-test was possible for Chemistry-II: the TSBIE Basic Learning Material on hand is physics-only and first-year, and no second-year chemistry paper is in the corpus. BOOK ERROR CORRECTED (book p.80, VSAQ 8): the book prints the zinc oxide ore as "Zincate - ZnO". The ore is ZINCITE, ZnO; a zincate is the [Zn(OH)₄]²⁻ ion formed when zinc or zinc oxide dissolves in alkali, and it is not a mineral. The card writes zincite and records the book's printed name in the step's why. BOOK SPELLING: the book prints "Heamatite"; it is written haematite here.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Ores of Al and Zn
steps.why: The question asks for ores with formulae, so a name on its own is not the answer. The book prints the zinc oxide ore as "Zincate"; the ore is zincite, ZnO, and a zincate is the [Zn(OH)₄]²⁻ ion in alkaline solution. The corrected name is written here.
common_mistakes: Writing zincate for ZnO. The ore is zincite; a zincate is an ion in solution.
Writing bauxite as Al₂O₃ only. The water of hydration is part of the formula: Al₂O₃·2H₂O.
steps.memory_tip: Zinc has two ores that both begin with zinc: zincite ZnO and zinc blende ZnS.
steps.margin_note: The formulae carry the mark here, not the names. Write each name with its formula beside it.

steps.label: Ores of Fe and Cu

lines.text: Copper pyrites CuFeS₂ is also a Cu ore

steps.why: Magnetite is Fe₃O₄ and haematite is Fe₂O₃, so the two iron ores differ only in the subscripts and that is where the mark is lost. Copper pyrites CuFeS₂ is the ore most copper is actually extracted from, so it is worth naming here as a third choice.
common_mistakes: Writing magnetite as Fe₂O₃. That is haematite; magnetite is Fe₃O₄.
Writing copper glance as CuS. Copper is in the +1 state, so it is Cu₂S.
steps.memory_tip: Haematite has two irons, magnetite has three. Cuprite is the oxide, copper glance the sulphide.
steps.margin_note: Two ores per metal is what the question asks for, so the four names with their formulae are the mark. Copper pyrites is worth knowing but earns nothing extra here.

insider_note: Eight formulae carry this question. The two most often written wrongly are magnetite Fe₃O₄ and zincite ZnO, which the book itself prints as "zincate".
